questions.question: Compare biometric authentication mechanisms by explaining how iris scanning and fingerprint recognition differ in terms of user interaction requirements and susceptibility to physical obstructions or spoofing.

marking_points.point: Iris scanning requires no physical contact from the user, whereas fingerprint scanning typically requires direct touch.
marking_points.quote: No touch required

marking_points.point: Fingerprint recognition is susceptible to failure due to temporary physical conditions such as dirt, grime, or wounds on the finger.
marking_points.quote: Dirt , grime and wounds

marking_points.point: Fingerprint systems are vulnerable to spoofing attacks, necessitating liveness detection measures to ensure the finger is real.
marking_points.quote: Can be spoofed – liveness                                              important!

marking_points.point: Iris scanning overcomes specific issues associated with retinal scanners, offering a different technical advantage in the biometric category.

marking_points.point: The placement of the finger is a critical factor for successful fingerprint capture, representing a procedural constraint not present in iris scanning.

marking_points.point: Iris patterns are coloured and visible from a distance, allowing for identification without the close-proximity constraints often needed for fingerprints.

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Explain the roles of the two primary system components in the Next Generation Secure Computing Base architecture.

marking_points.point: Nexus acts as a special kernel that is the core of the trusted operating system, aiming to isolate normal and trusted modes differently in memory.
marking_points.quote: Special kernel (core of the trusted operating) Goal: Isolate the process of normal mode and trusted mode differently in memory

marking_points.point: Nexus authenticates and protects data entered, stored, communicated, and displayed by using data encryption.
marking_points.quote: Functionality: Authenticate and protect data (entered, stored, communicated, and displayed) by data encryption

marking_points.point: The Nexus Computing Agent is a trusted software component that runs in trusted mode and communicates with Nexus.
marking_points.quote: Trusted software component Runs in trusted mode that communicates with Nexus

marking_points.point: The specifications for the Nexus Computing Agent are open-source, allowing developers to create their own agents for the trusted platform.
marking_points.quote: Open-source for NCA specifications Developers can make their own agents to run on the trusted platform

marking_points.point: Nexus serves as an application interface to the TPM, enabling secure interactions between applications and the hardware module.
marking_points.quote: Application interface to TPM

marking_points.point: Nexus ensures security by not trusting the OS, thereby maintaining the integrity of the trusted computing environment.
marking_points.quote: Does not trust OS

questions.question: Describe six key aspects of Windows security mechanisms, including their design goals, access control capabilities, subject management, and potential vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: DACLs enable fine-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Active Directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads, with security credentials stored in a token.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads. Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: Access rights are encoded as a 32-bit mask, including standard rights like DELETE and READ_CONTROL.
marking_points.quote: Encoded as a 32-bit mask Standard access rights: common to most object types DELETE READ_CONTROL: read object’s security descriptor

questions.question: Explain the structural characteristics and operational implications of Access Control Matrices, Access Control Lists, and Capabilities as mechanisms for implementing access policies.

marking_points.point: The Access Control Matrix is a basic control structure that offers clarity of definition and ease of verification but suffers from poor scalability and poor handling of changes.
marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure. Advantages: clarity of deﬁnition easy to verify Disadvantages: poor scalability poor handling of changes

marking_points.point: Access Control Lists provide an object-centered description of access rights which allows for easy access to object access rights and relative easiness of management using abstractions.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights: Advantages: easy access to object access rights relative easiness of management using abstractions

marking_points.point: Access Control Lists suffer from disadvantages including poor overview of access rights per subject, difficulty of revocation, and difficulty of sharing.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor overview of access rights per subject difﬁculty of revocation difﬁculty of sharing

marking_points.point: Capabilities are listed alongside ACLs and ACMs as one of the primary structures used for implementing access control policies.
marking_points.quote: Structures Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: Most common practical access control instruments include ACLs, capabilities, and various abstractions to implement policies controlling subject-object access.
marking_points.quote: Most common practical access control instruments are ACLs, capabilities and various abstractions.

marking_points.point: Effective access control structures must meet requirements such as the ability to express control policies, verifiability of correctness, and scalability and manageability.
marking_points.quote: Requirements for access control structures: an ability to express control policies veriﬁability of correctness. scalability and manageability

questions.question: Discuss the propagation mechanisms and operational characteristics of computer worms, referencing historical examples and their impact on network infrastructure.

marking_points.point: Worms are self-replicating code that can propagate automatically across networks by exploiting vulnerabilities in remote systems.
marking_points.quote: Viruses and self-replicating code

marking_points.point: The Morris worm demonstrated large-scale propagation by using a debugging feature of sendmail to penetrate thousands of computers on the Arpanet.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution) Propagated in the Arpanet Penetrated ca.6,000 computers (10% of Arpanet)

marking_points.point: Malware such as rootkits ensures privileged remote access by masking malicious processes to stay hidden from detection software.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Early theoretical foundations for malware propagation were established through mathematical descriptions of virus replication and survival strategies.
marking_points.quote: Mathematical description of virus propagation To increase their survival chances, programs can replicate themselves

marking_points.point: Attacks exploit system vulnerabilities, which are defined as weaknesses that can be leveraged to damage assets or gain unauthorized control.
marking_points.quote: Vulnerability: weakness of a system Threat: object, person, or other entity representing a constant danger to an asset Attack: a deliberate act that exploits vulnerability

marking_points.point: The disruption class of threats involves the interruption or prevention of correct operation, often resulting from attacks like denial of service.
marking_points.quote: Disruption - interruption or prevention of correct operation Modification Integrity services counter this threat Usurpation - unauthorized control of some part of a system Modification, spoofing, delay, denial of service Availability services counter this threat

questions.question: Discuss the operational characteristics and propagation mechanism of the Samy Worm, explaining how it exploited user profiles to infect other users.

marking_points.point: The worm injected JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It retrieved the list of the victim's friends by performing a GET request on the user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: The malware added itself as a friend by performing an XML-HTTP request on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile would have their own profile and friends list infected with the worm.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The attack resulted in the infection of approximately one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The worm demonstrated how cross-site scripting allows dynamic injection via user requests rather than originating from the web server.
marking_points.quote: In a XSS attack, Javascript does not originate from a web server but is dynamically injected into it via a user request a following reﬂection from a third-party, a “cross-site”.

questions.question: Explain six preventive network security mechanisms that organizations can implement to enhance their security posture, detailing the specific function or advantage of each.

marking_points.point: Firewalls control traffic based on predetermined policies
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation creates boundaries between segments with assets sharing common functions or roles

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access restricts users to only the permissions required for their specific role

marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: The Simple Security Rule allows access only if the object is in the same company dataset as previously accessed objects or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

is in the same company datasets as                                                the objects already accessed by s,                                                        that is, “within the Wall,” or
belongs to an entirely different                                           conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The *-property restricts write access to prevent information flow from a higher sensitivity level to a lower one within the context of the wall.
marking_points.quote:
Write access is only permitted if:
access is permitted by the simple                                     security rule, and
no object can be read which is:
in a different company dataset than the                                                  one for which write access is requested,                                                                   and
contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is strictly an access control confidentiality policy designed to address conflicts of interest rather than being an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: The Bell-La Padula model focuses on confidentiality through its simple security property (no read up) and *-property (no write down).
marking_points.quote:
Simple Security Rule: A subject s can be granted access to an object o only if the object:
is in the same company datasets as                                                the objects already accessed by s,                                                        that is, “within the Wall,” or
belongs to an entirely different                                           conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The Biba model focuses on integrity, ensuring that subjects cannot read from lower integrity levels and cannot write to higher integrity levels.
